---
title: "TAF readiness"
---

The [TAF readiness level](../system/readiness-level.qmd) of the stock assessment repositories in [ices-taf](https://github.com/ices-taf), by assessment year.

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_plot.R")

repos <- read.csv("../_generated/taf-repos.csv")

assessments <- readiness_assessments(repos)
# shared by the chart and the table so that clicking a bar filters the table
shared <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(assessments)

n <- table(assessments$Level)
at_least <- function(level) sum(repos$trl >= level, na.rm = TRUE)
untested <- sum(repos$trl %in% 1 & !repos$qc_tested)
```

There are `r nrow(repos)` stock assessment repositories.

- `r at_least(1)` have reached level 1, with their code on GitHub.
- `r at_least(2)` of those have reached level 2, passing the QC test. `r untested` of the repositories at level 1 have not been tested.
- None has been tested for level 3 yet.
- `r n[["No level"]]` have no level, because they have no modelling in them: no R script or R Markdown file with `model` or `method` in its name, or only an empty `model.R`.

`r sum(repos$published)` of the repositories are for stocks published in [ices-advice](https://github.com/ices-advice), which is to have a public repository there: `r sum(repos$published & repos$trl %in% 2)` at level 2, `r sum(repos$published & repos$trl %in% 1)` at level 1 and `r sum(repos$published & is.na(repos$trl))` with no level.

The QC results are from `r format(as.Date(max(repos$qc_date, na.rm = TRUE)), "%e %B %Y")`.

The last column of the table is what was found of the link to GitHub in the [advice sheet](advice-sheets.qmd) of the stock, for the advice from 2024 on.

The green blocks in the panel of the not published are the published assessments of the year, drawn on top so that its bars show all the assessments of each year. The assessments with no level are left out of the chart to begin with: click **No level** in the legend to add them, and again to take them out. They are always in the table.

Click a bar to list its assessments in the table below. To show them all again, use the button above the table or double-click the chart.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
readiness_chart(assessments, shared)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
show_all_button(shared, "Show all assessments")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
DT::datatable(
  shared,
  rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE,
  options = list(pageLength = 25, order = list(list(0, "desc"), list(1, "asc")))
)
```

## Other repositories

The readiness level of the repositories of four other types of work, by the year in their name. The levels are found in the same way as for the assessments: level 1 for a repository with some modelling in it, and level 2 for one that also passes the QC test. These repositories are not published themselves, so there is no panel for the published.

```{r}
#| include: false
other <- read.csv("../_generated/other-repos.csv")
other$level <- factor(ifelse(is.na(other$trl), 0, other$trl), 0:4, readiness_levels)
# in the order of the panels
other$group <- factor(other$group, unique(c("Mixed fisheries advice", "Benchmarks", "Reference points", "Surveys", other$group)))
# the levels in the order they are stacked and listed, those with no level last
stacked <- c(setdiff(levels(droplevels(other$level)), "No level"), "No level")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
types <- tapply(other$type, other$group, function(x) paste0("`", sort(unique(x)), "`", collapse = ", "))
summary <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(other$group, droplevels(other$level))[, stacked, drop = FALSE])
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Group = rownames(summary),
    Types = unname(types[rownames(summary)]),
    Repositories = rowSums(summary),
    summary,
    "Not tested" = as.vector(table(other$group, !other$qc_tested)[rownames(summary), "TRUE"]),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", "l", rep("r", ncol(summary) + 2))
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 7
# the repositories, shared by the chart and the table so that clicking a bar
# filters the table
other_listed <- data.frame(
  Year = other$year,
  Repository = sprintf("<a href=\"https://github.com/ices-taf/%s\">%s</a>", other$name, other$name),
  Group = other$group,
  Type = other$type,
  Level = other$level,
  QC = ifelse(!other$qc_tested, "Not tested", ifelse(other$qc_passed, "Passed", "Failed"))
)
names(other_listed)[6] <- "QC test"
other_shared <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(other_listed)

# the bars: the number of repositories by group, year and level, stacked by
# hand so that a clicked bar is highlighted in place, each with the keys of
# its repositories. Those with no level are at the top of a bar, and left
# out until clicked in the legend, as in the chart of the assessments.
bars <- aggregate(
  list(key = other_shared$key()),
  list(level = other$level, year = other$year, group = other$group),
  function(x) I(list(x))
)
bars$n <- lengths(bars$key)
bars <- bars[order(bars$group, bars$year, match(bars$level, stacked)), ]
bars$base <- ave(bars$n, bars$group, bars$year, FUN = function(n) cumsum(n) - n)

# a level has its entry in the legend from the first panel it is in
groups <- levels(other$group)
first <- vapply(stacked, function(level) groups[groups %in% bars$group[bars$level == level]][1], "")

panel <- function(group) {
  p <- plot_ly()
  for (level in stacked) {
    d <- bars[bars$group == group & bars$level == level, ]
    if (!nrow(d)) next
    p <- p |>
      add_bars(
        data = linked_bars(d, other_shared),
        x = ~year, y = ~n, base = ~base, name = level,
        legendgroup = level, showlegend = first[[level]] == group,
        legendrank = match(level, stacked),
        visible = if (level == "No level") "legendonly" else TRUE,
        marker = list(color = readiness_colours[[level]], line = list(color = "white", width = 2)),
        customdata = ~n, hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{customdata} repositories"
      )
  }
  p |>
    layout(
      barmode = "overlay",
      xaxis = list(title = "", dtick = 1, range = range(other$year) + c(-0.6, 0.6)),
      yaxis = list(title = "", rangemode = "nonnegative")
    )
}

title <- function(text, k) {
  list(
    text = paste0("<b>", text, "</b>"), showarrow = FALSE,
    x = 0, xref = paste0("x", if (k %% 2 == 0) 2 else "", " domain"), xanchor = "left",
    y = 1, yref = paste0("y", if (k > 1) k else "", " domain"), yanchor = "bottom"
  )
}

subplot(lapply(groups, panel), nrows = 2, shareX = TRUE, margin = c(0.03, 0.03, 0.07, 0.07)) |>
  taf_layout(
    annotations = lapply(seq_along(groups), function(k) title(groups[k], k)),
    margin = list(t = 40)
  ) |>
  layout(legend = list(y = -0.08, traceorder = "normal")) |>
  highlight(
    on = "plotly_click", off = "plotly_doubleclick", opacityDim = 0.35,
    selected = attrs_selected(showlegend = FALSE)
  ) |>
  config(doubleClickDelay = 500)
```

The repositories are those named `<year>_<name>_<type>` with these types. The chart opens without those with no level: click **No level** in the legend to add them. Each panel has its own scale.

Click a bar to list its repositories in the table at the end of the page. To show them all again, use the button above the table or double-click the chart.


```{r}
#| echo: false
show_all_button(other_shared, "Show all repositories")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
DT::datatable(

  options = list(pageLength = 25, order = list(list(0, "desc"), list(2, "asc"), list(1, "asc")))
)
```
